long_biography.plain_text:
After nearly four decades in the family textile business, Sabancı left his executive responsibilities and tried retirement. Within days he reconsidered. Encouraged by friends and relatives already active at sea, he studied the sector and chose international merchant transport as a new operating focus.

His first acquisition was financed through long-term overseas shipping credit, a model he used to commission modern, high-capacity ships from Asian yards. The resulting platform grew rapidly while his legacy Sabancı Holding and Akbank shares remained intact. Sabancı set his ambitions against established Greek owners, pursuing scale in a sector he entered in his mid-fifties.
